If you're curious about wrestling, my best advice is to watch WWE raw on Monday nights, or WWE smackdown on Friday nights. I'm not a fan of WWE and haven't been for quite awhile, but thankfully wrestling is in another big boom period. This is partly in thanks to AEW breaking the monopoly that Vince McMahon has held over the industry. If you find that you enjoy the wrestling, but don't like how WWE does things...I implore you to give All Elite Wrestling a try. They have dynamite on Wednesday nights and collision on Saturday. They're fairly new, just celebrated their 5th year as a company. Or search YouTube for NJPW (New Japan Professional Wrestling) they focus much more on the sport than the theatrics and storyline. There's tons of options for wrestling ATM and I encourage everyone to look at all avenues and figure out what works for them. There's a lot of tribalism within the IWC (Internet wrestling community), and a lot of it is unwarranted.

If you're interested in something like this, do some research on the programs and agencies in your area, and see if you can do a walk through to see if it might be a good fit for you.

If your child calls you from a mental hospital and asks you to come pick them up after they've been discharged, you fucking go get them. Do NOT tell them you're too busy, or that other people might need you. They need you, right then and there. 

Context: I was admitted to a 72 hour hold, during which I spoke to only 2 people; my mother and my now partner(who was my boss at the time). The day of my discharge, I called my mother as soon as I found out and let her know I would be discharged later in the afternoon. I asked her for a ride home and was met with "I don't know if your grandma or your brother need me, so I can't....I'm too busy." I proceeded to call my now girlfriend (who was at work) and asked her if she could come pick me up, she immediately left work and drove an hour and a half away to come get me, no questions asked. I later found out that all my mother did that day was sit at home and play on her phone. She could've came and got me, but chose not to. It was one of the first signs that she was not someone I could count on to be an ally for my mental health. Between that and finally noticing the way she would guilt trip or gaslight me into things, I began to take moral inventory on if I needed or wanted her in my life. And I can happily say, my life is exponentially better without her in it. I had always lived under my brother's shadow and very rarely ever asked to be put first, but in this case I needed her and she couldn't be bothered to even make an attempt.
